text: Build small. Finish often. Learn from what survives contact with reality.
A useful question is often the first working prototype.
Debugging is detective work where you are also the suspect.
Consistency makes the impressive thing look inevitable.
Make it work. Understand why. Then make it better.
The fastest way to learn a tool is to build something slightly too ambitious with it.
Every clean solution started as a messy question.
Don't just collect tutorials. Collect finished experiments.
Progress is a trail of problems you can solve now that you couldn't solve before.
The best feature is the one that makes the user's next step easier.
Be curious enough to explore and disciplined enough to ship.
Readable code is a kindness to your future self.
Start with what you know. Use the project to discover what you don't.
A failure that taught you something is part of the build history.
Keep the scope small enough to finish and interesting enough to care.
One solved edge case can teach more than ten copied examples.
The terminal is quiet. The possibilities are not.
Good engineering is curiosity with a feedback loop.
If you can explain the trade-off, you are closer to owning the solution.
Keep your experiments honest, your notes clear, and your commits small.
